title: Navigating Market Chaos - Systematic Investor 336

meta.source: Macro Transcripts/Navigating Market Chaos - Systematic Investor 336.docx

summary: Systematic Investor 336: Niels and Graham Robertson on early-2025 trend performance, alternative markets, trend design (crossover vs breakout), portable alpha, and long-short quality as a defensive partner. Conclusion: diversification of price drivers drives trend Sharpe; trend and quality hedge different crisis speeds.

coverage.note: Intro, sponsor disclaimers, small talk about young people and geopolitics: nothing actionable
Trend start to 2025 mixed by sector; US gold reserve repricing idea
Coffee, JGB widow trade, DAX, gold-Treasury link, EU equities, European energy
OTC liquidity, Nord Pool diversification, Swiss swaps
Trend dispersion, 2025 liquid markets, diversification long vs short term, alternative markets trend timing
Sqrt(N) Sharpe, alternative vs liquid markets, crisis alpha, hedge instruments
Alt-market liquidity and crowding, CDS stress liquidity, crypto exit risk
Crypto bubbles, risk diversification, trend barometer, CTA index performance
Crossover advantages, breakout models, design choices, Dunn history
Volatility breakout history, Taxi driver problem (Mag 7)
Portable alpha, crisis alpha, margin management
Trend replacing bonds, issuance, equity falls, 2022
Vol targeting, Bitcoin vol, deleveraging, DeepSeek
Long-short quality as partner, lines of defence, tech concentration, price vs value

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: opportunities in some sectors for sure you know like equities but then kind of those opportunities been somewhat canceled out uh in other sectors um currency Springs to mind
claims.claim: Early 2025 trend following was mixed: equity trends offset by currency losses, with bonds in between, so sector-level dispersion drives CTA returns.
claims.testable: partly: sector P&L attribution is checkable but this is one two-month window

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: if they Mark to Market that instead of the $42 per ounce which I think is the official price
claims.claim: Repricing US gold reserves from the official $42/oz to market would create a large balance-sheet asset to lend against (sovereign wealth fund idea), a catalyst supporting the gold trend.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: we have a new cocoa because last year it was all about cocoa this year it's all about coffee so we see some challenges with the um with the crop coming out for next year
claims.claim: A lower coffee crop (estimated 4-5% below) is pushing coffee prices up, giving trend followers a new soft-commodity trend after cocoa.
claims.testable: partly: crop estimates are data but one-off supply shock

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: the Widow trade is something that has been Des used to be to describe trying to go short Japanese government bonds um for a long time because every time you tried the boj would basically make you pay
claims.claim: The widow-maker short JGB trade (previously punished by BoJ intervention) began paying for trend followers once JGB 10y yield rose from -0.25% to 1.44% since Sept 2024, a policy regime shift.
claims.testable: yes: JGB yield trend vs trend signal P&L

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: the Dax index is made up as far as I know of a lot of multinational uh companies that are making um money at the moment
claims.claim: The DAX trended up despite weak German economy because its constituents are multinationals earning abroad, so index trends can diverge from local macro.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: you look at the effect of one market and what should that do to another market and you can capture Trends in lots of different ways
claims.claim: Trading many markets globally lets a trend follower capture cross-market knock-on effects, e.g. gold repricing changing Treasury issuance and hence bond trends.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: European Equity markets are on fire this year is is amazing given the the noise that's
claims.claim: European equities rallied despite tariff headlines, showing market prices can decouple from economic news, which suits price-based trend rules.
claims.testable: partly: price momentum testable, news decoupling is anecdotal

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: you've got very low inventories you've got very cold weather
claims.claim: European gas and power trended up in early 2025 because of low inventories, very cold weather and little wind output from German renewables, a supply shock after a range-bound 2024.
claims.indicator: EU gas/power prices, inventories, wind output
claims.direction: long European natural gas and power
claims.testable: partly: inventories and weather are data

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: there's liquidity off exchange that you can potentially capture um some of it is OTC um over the counter which on First Sight you know people think OTC equals a liquid that's not necessarily the case
claims.claim: OTC and off-exchange markets can be traded at size with some human execution and ISDA arrangements, so low exchange-visible liquidity is not a barrier to adding markets.
claims.conditions: needs OTC execution capability and legal agreements

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: the thing that drives the price of a Scandinavian hydroelectric Market is weather patterns it's how much rain is falling so the trends you get in those markets are just completely diversifying
claims.claim: Markets with idiosyncratic drivers (Nord Pool hydro power driven by rainfall) give trends uncorrelated with macro markets, and more distinct price drivers improve trend-following diversification.
claims.testable: partly: correlation of Nord Pool trend P&L to other markets is testable

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: the Swiss National Bank opened up the prospects of going Subzero rates again and that's something that of course would drive up the price of those instruments
claims.claim: Swiss interest-rate swaps, untradable via futures, allowed trend capture of SNB sub-zero rate prospects, an example of alternative markets adding return sources.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: how long does it have to go up how long does it have to be go down which markets are you talking about how are you measuring it these things introduce huge variations
claims.claim: Design choices (lookback, market set, measurement) create huge dispersion between trend managers, who can be up and down over the same period.
claims.testable: yes: dispersion across lookbacks and universes can be measured

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: the very biggest liquid markets really nicely trended uh particularly in a relatively slow point of view
claims.claim: After the US election (Dec 2024-Jan 2025) the largest liquid markets trended well for slower signals, while smaller diversifiers had not helped over the previous couple of years.
claims.indicator: slow trend signals on liquid futures

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: we know in the long term when we run a simulation diversification tends to play out in the short term kind of anything goes
claims.claim: Diversification across markets pays off in long-run simulation but over short periods anything can happen, a communication problem with investors.
claims.testable: yes: compare diversified vs concentrated trend over rolling windows

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: they don't trend better they just Trend at different times
claims.claim: Alternative markets (per other managers' study) do not trend better than liquid futures, they trend at different times, which is the diversification benefit.
claims.indicator: trend P&L of alternative vs liquid markets
claims.testable: yes: compare trend Sharpe by market group

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: your sharp ratio increases with something like the square root of the number of markets you can get a 0.1 sharp up to one sharp by trading 100 completely independent markets
claims.claim: With uncorrelated markets, Sharpe scales with the square root of the number of markets (0.1 each -> 1.0 with 100), so adding independent price drivers raises long-run trend Sharpe.
claims.conditions: only if markets are truly uncorrelated
claims.testable: yes: sqrt(N) law vs realised correlations

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: if you look at the sharp ratio of alternative markets it tends to look better in the long term I would argue because the diversification is better
claims.claim: Alternative markets show a higher long-run Sharpe, attributed to better diversification rather than stronger trending.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: the classic Futures markets seem to have a a lower long-term Shar ratio but that crisis Alpha property for which people really look to our strategies tends to come out stronger
claims.claim: Liquid futures (S&P, Treasuries) have a lower long-run Sharpe but stronger crisis alpha (2008, 2022) since they are susceptible to central bank and macro events.
claims.testable: yes: crisis-window returns by market group

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: you probably want to be trading the kind of instruments that you'd have in that risky asset like S&P is a classic example treasuries is an example
claims.claim: To hedge a risk-asset portfolio, trade the same instruments held in it (equity indices, Treasuries), not unrelated markets like Scandinavian power.
claims.testable: partly: hedge effectiveness by instrument group testable

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: the alternative markets if you look at them on a market by market basis they're not necessarily smaller than Futures markets they're harder to access but not necessarily smaller
claims.claim: Alternative markets are harder to access, not smaller, and are sized with the same liquidity rules as futures; smaller markets just get smaller position size.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: pick it up in terms of transaction costs increasing um but you don't necessarily see that
claims.claim: Crowding in alternative markets would show up as rising transaction costs; internal costs and independent surveys of credit derivative and swap market size show markets still growing.
claims.testable: yes: track execution costs over time

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: credit derivative when when times get stressy what you often see is is the demand for insurance
claims.claim: Credit derivative liquidity does not dry up in stress because demand for credit insurance rises and market size grows.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: we had a little bit of a crypto crash earlier this month
claims.claim: Crypto has exit-liquidity risk: ether fell over 20% in one day on a weekend when futures could not trade, an issue to price into position sizing.
claims.testable: partly: gap risk can be modelled

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: Trend following strategies love Bubbles and anything where there is just very little idea of fundamental value has this this propensity to form Bubbles
claims.claim: Assets with no anchor for fundamental value (crypto) tend to form bubbles, which are favourable for trend followers.
claims.testable: partly: crypto trend backtest short history

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: you diversify across as many future strategies uh Futures markets as you can
claims.claim: Risk from crypto is managed by diversifying across many futures markets and across coins; investor appetite, not opportunity, can limit allocation.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: my own Trend barometer um finished at 30 yesterday which is weak uh on the weak side and but I think also people should always uh remember that it is using somewhat shorter term time frames
claims.claim: Host's Trend Barometer (30, weak) uses shorter timeframes so it tracks the Short-Term Traders Index, which was weak.
claims.testable: yes: barometer value vs subsequent CTA returns

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: btop 50 was up 56 basis points for the month up 1.78% for the year so gen CTA index pretty much flat up 11 basis points for the month
claims.claim: Performance data to 25 Feb 2025: BTOP50 +1.78% YTD, SG CTA +0.73%, SG Trend +0.56%, STI -0.25%, versus MSCI World +5.37%, S&P 500 +4.64%.
claims.indicator: BTOP50, SG CTA, SG Trend, Short-Term Traders Index

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: I think the original signals were were kind of binary you know it's it's on if it's going up or it's off or it's it's it's minus one if it's going down
claims.claim: Early trend signals were binary (+1/-1); evolution to smoother moving-average crossovers allows gradual position changes.
claims.direction: long when up, short when down
claims.testable: yes: binary vs smooth signal backtest

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: the SG Trend index utili and I think it's the Trend indicator that you're referring to utilizes the 20 and 120 day crossover as a trigger
claims.claim: The SG Trend Indicator uses a 20/120-day moving average crossover, chosen as best fit to the index over years, but manager dispersion is huge so one tool cannot represent them.
claims.testable: yes: replicate index with the crossover

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: the beauty of a system like that is that they're smooth they're incremental and any kind of positions that you put on
claims.claim: Moving-average crossover positions change smoothly and incrementally, so market impact and transaction costs are low.
claims.testable: yes: turnover and cost comparison vs breakouts

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: breakout models where you effectively form a channel round about a price and then if the price moves upside on the upside
claims.claim: Breakout (channel) models go long when price exits a channel upward and short on a downside break; back-returns are another trend measure.
claims.direction: long on upside breakout, short on downside

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: do you use a fixed window you know that 20 120-day uh that the trend indicator uses you know is that just a constant window
claims.claim: Crossover design choices include fixed windows versus weighting recent observations, which makes the signal more reactive.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: at da we actually started using volatility breakout that's back in the early ' 70s um we never we never used uh moving averages
claims.claim: Dunn used volatility breakout from the early 1970s and never moving averages, later adding continuous time-series momentum; trend systems have long histories (Donchian four-week rule 1960, Turtles 1984).

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: which is more volatility breakout um and average true range
claims.claim: Bollinger bands and average true range are volatility-breakout measures, used by Dunn and Campbell since the early 1970s, preceding the dates found in the literature.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: it's very difficult to beat a dominant performer in an index so the mag s being the classic case in the US driving everything
claims.claim: The taxi driver problem: a few dominant, well-known stocks (Magnificent 7, Novo Nordisk) drive index returns, so diversified investors feel they underperform and clients ask for solutions.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: let's separate our stock Pickers problem into a kind of beta part you're just run perform in line with the index with an alpha part which is a kind of long short stock Pickers problem
claims.claim: Portable alpha: take equity beta at index weight and port the alpha to other sources (quant, multi-strategy, trend) away from pure equities to diversify alpha sources.
claims.testable: yes: overlay backtest of index plus trend

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: when your beta portfolio is drawing down your Alpha if it's Trend fing tends to do quite well via this crisis Alpha property
claims.claim: Trend as the alpha leg tends to gain when the equity beta leg draws down (crisis alpha), reducing joint-drawdown and margin problems.
claims.indicator: trend vs equity correlation in drawdown
claims.testable: yes: trend returns in equity drawdowns

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: margin management can be very tricky you got to make sure that your Alpha strategy isn't drawing down at the same time as your beta strategy
claims.claim: Portable alpha needs margin management: the alpha strategy must not draw down while beta draws down.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: it always comes back when equities are doing really well and and we have to come up with a solution as to what why we're how how can you participate in Trend
claims.claim: Interest in portable alpha is cyclical, resurfacing when equities do very well and clients feel they underperform.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: it's not going to be cheaper for for countries to defend themselves so you would think that there's a lot of bond issuance coming
claims.claim: Higher defence spending implies more government bond issuance, so the bigger portfolio risk may be in bonds (yield rises), prompting interest in trend as a fixed-income replacement.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: equities you look at msci world has lost about half their value twice since 2000 you know the the tech bubble bursting 2000 GFC 2008 and then of course you've got covid
claims.claim: Trend following has a crisis-alpha record in equity falls (MSCI World lost about half twice since 2000, about 30% in Covid).
claims.indicator: MSCI World drawdowns vs trend index
claims.testable: yes: trend index returns in these windows

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: 2022 showed that that wasn't the case and it's definitely rekindled interest in a dynamic strategy like trendl where you can be sure bonds you can be short equities
claims.claim: Bond hedging of equities failed in 2022; a dynamic strategy that can short bonds restored interest in trend as a defensive allocation.
claims.direction: trend allocation instead of static bonds

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: you can do a five Vol strategy you can do a 10 Vol strategy you can do a 20 volt strategy it it it's just the turn of a dial it doesn't really change anything
claims.claim: Trend strategies can be run at any volatility target (5, 10, 20) by scaling a dial; investor preferences differ and asset volatility does not matter.
claims.testable: yes: scale-invariance of Sharpe to vol target

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: bitcoin as an example again you know you've got an asset class that trades on around about 100 V doesn't bother for us at all it just means that we need a smaller amount of it
claims.claim: High-volatility assets (Bitcoin about 100 vol) are handled by smaller position size under volatility-based sizing.
claims.direction: smaller position when vol is high

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: there was a general deleveraging uh in our industry compared to say the '90s and the 80s uh leverage and vola came down
claims.claim: Trend funds delevered after the GFC as investors wanted low-vol products; with higher rates and vol, some investors may now want more return.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: Donald Trump called it a a wakeup call for us companies
claims.claim: The DeepSeek shock on 27 Jan 2025 triggered a tech sell-off and a Sputnik-moment narrative, but Mag 7 stocks bounced back.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: long short quality a cash Equity strategy where you go long high
claims.claim: Long-short quality (QMJ) paid in flights to quality when trend struggled (SVB 2023, yen carry unwind Q3 2024), a partner for trend.
claims.direction: long high quality, short low quality
claims.testable: yes: QMJ returns in event windows vs CTA returns

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: Trend requires sustained sell-offs typically to work to to exhibit these crisis Alpha periods typically I guess of the order of weeks to months
claims.claim: Lines of defence: trend needs sustained sell-offs over weeks to months, while long-short quality responds more immediately, like a long-volatility strategy.

claims.speaker: Graham Robertson
claims.quote: you tend to find that they're often dominated by technology stocks software and services semi semiconductors and Equipment
claims.claim: Quality stocks are concentrated in technology; on the DeepSeek tech sell-off the quality factor did not sell off, and in 2000-03 simulations quality did OK, so tech-concentration risk looks limited.
claims.testable: yes: QMJ returns in tech sell-offs

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: there is a disconnect uh between the price and and what we Define as value
claims.claim: Host: price has become disconnected from traditional value (Bitcoin worth zero or millions), which argues for price-only approaches.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: be a good idea to just focus on price because that's the one thing we do know
claims.claim: If value is subjective, strategies focused only on price such as trend following may have more opportunity and investors are more open to them.
